DIET AND NUTRITION OVERVIEW
  OBJECTIVE: Support pregnancy-related energy needs, promote lean mass retention, and optimize recovery, while ensuring adequate micronutrients for both mother and fetus.

MACROS
  - Estimated daily calories: maintain weight or moderate gain depending on pre-pregnancy body weight and physician guidance; generally 300-450 kcal/day above nonpregnant maintenance in 2nd/3rd trimesters is common, adjust by weight trajectory and clinician.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (adjust to appetite and tolerance). High-quality sources: lean meats, fish with low mercury, eggs, dairy, legumes, soy, quinoa, and protein supplements if approved.
  - Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day depending on activity; focus on complex carbs around training window; fiber 25–35 g/day.
  - Fats: include healthy fats; essential omega-3s (DHA/EPA) 200–300 mg/day; include oily fish 2x/week or trusted supplementation per clinician guidance.
  - Hydration: aim for 2.3–3.0 L/day fluids, more with heat or exercise.

NUTRITION TIMING
  - Pre-workout meal: 30–60 minutes before training; 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs; example: yogurt with fruit, or oats with milk and berries.
  - Post-workout: within 1–2 hours; 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs to support recovery.
  - Consistent protein each meal: distribute 20–40 g protein across 4–6 meals to support lean mass and fetal needs.
  - Iron and calcium: prioritize iron-rich foods (red meat, lentils, fortified cereals) and calcium (dairy, fortified plant milks, leafy greens); consider clinician-recommended supplements if needed.
  - Vitamin D, folate, iodine: ensure intake meets prenatal guidelines; supplement as advised by OB.

FOOD SENSITIVITIES AND TGO
  - Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mish, etc.) or limit per clinician.
  - Limit processed foods; prioritize whole foods to support satiety and micronutrient intake.
  - Mindful of nausea; if appetite is low, smaller frequent meals with easy-to-digest options.

SUPPLEMENTATION (as appropriate per clinician)
  - Prenatal vitamin daily (folate, iron, iodine, DHA as per guidance)
  - Vitamin D as recommended (often 600–1000 IU/day; adjust per levels)
  - Iron if deficiency risk: ferritin-based dosing under supervision
  - Probiotics if advised for GI comfort

TRAINING-NUTRITION SYNC
  - Adjust calories upward on training days if appetite supports; otherwise maintain baseline but ensure protein targets are met.
  - Hydration around training: add 300–500 ml of fluids during workouts if sweating.

MEAL PLAN FRAMEWORK
  - Breakfast: 25–40 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrates, fats moderate
  - Lunch: 30–40 g protein, 60–90 g carbs, fats moderate
  - Snack: 15–25 g protein, 20–40 g carbs
  - Dinner: 30–40 g protein, 40–70 g carbs, fats moderate
  - Evening option: if hungry, light snack focusing on protein and fiber

MONITORING AND SAFETY
  - Track weight gain trajectory per prenatal guidelines; adjust caloric intake if weight gain is faster or slower than target.
  - Monitor energy, nausea, heartburn, and exercise tolerance; modify training volume or food timing as needed.
  - Avoid supine positions after 16 weeks; ensure diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor engagement during core work.
  - Maintain safe intensity: RPE targets as previously established; avoid max efforts.

DIET AND NUTRITION OVERVIEW
  OBJECTIVE: Support pregnancy-related energy needs, promote lean mass retention, and optimize recovery, while ensuring adequate micronutrients for both mother and fetus.

MACROS
  - Estimated daily calories: maintain weight or moderate gain depending on pre-pregnancy body weight and physician guidance; generally 300-450 kcal/day above nonpregnant maintenance in 2nd/3rd trimesters; adjust by weight trajectory and clinician.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (adjust to appetite and tolerance). High-quality sources: lean meats, fish with low mercury, eggs, dairy, legumes, soy, quinoa, and protein supplements if approved.
  - Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day depending on activity; focus on complex carbs around training window; fiber 25–35 g/day.
  - Fats: include healthy fats; essential omega-3s (DHA/EPA) 200–300 mg/day; include oily fish 2x/week or trusted supplementation per clinician guidance.
  - Hydration: aim for 2.3–3.0 L/day fluids, more with heat or exercise.

NUTRITION TIMING
  - Pre-workout meal: 30–60 minutes before training; 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs; example: yogurt with fruit, or oats with milk and berries.
  - Post-workout: within 1–2 hours; 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs to support recovery.
  - Consistent protein each meal: distribute 20–40 g protein across 4–6 meals to support lean mass and fetal needs.
  - Iron and calcium: prioritize iron-rich foods (red meat, lentils, fortified cereals) and calcium (dairy, fortified plant milks, leafy greens); consider clinician-recommended supplements if needed.
  - Vitamin D, folate, iodine: ensure intake meets prenatal guidelines; supplement as advised by OB.

FOOD SENSITIVITIES AND TGO
  - Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, etc.) or limit per clinician.
  - Limit processed foods; prioritize whole foods to support satiety and micronutrient intake.
  - Mindful of nausea; if appetite is low, smaller frequent meals with easy-to-digest options.

SUPPLEMENTATION (as appropriate per clinician)
  - Prenatal vitamin daily (folate, iron, iodine, DHA as per guidance)
  - Vitamin D as recommended (often 600–1000 IU/day; adjust per levels)
  - Iron if deficiency risk: ferritin-based dosing under supervision
  - Probiotics if advised for GI comfort

TRAINING-NUTRITION SYNC
  - Adjust calories upward on training days if appetite supports; otherwise maintain baseline but ensure protein targets are met.
  - Hydration around training: add 300–500 ml of fluids during workouts if sweating.

MEAL PLAN FRAMEWORK
  - Breakfast: 25–40 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrates, fats moderate
  - Lunch: 30–40 g protein, 60–90 g carbs, fats moderate
  - Snack: 15–25 g protein, 20–40 g carbs
  - Dinner: 30–40 g protein, 40–70 g carbs, fats moderate
  - Evening option: if hungry, light snack focusing on protein and fiber
